b1: This is Antares CRM, a customer relationship management web app for small businesses. In Settings, under Connections, a business connects its Instagram professional account.
b2: Clicking Connect Instagram starts the Instagram Business Login.
b3: Instagram shows the permissions Antares requests: view profile and access media, manage comments, and manage messages. The account owner reviews them and clicks Allow.
b4: Back in Antares, the account is connected. We use instagram_business_basic to show the account's name, username and profile picture, and to identify which account receives the messages and comments.
m1: In the Inbox, filtered to the Instagram channel, Antares lists the business account's Instagram conversations. Other customers' names are blurred for privacy.
m2: A customer sends a direct message to the business account. It arrives in Antares in real time, through the Instagram messaging webhook. The agent opens the conversation.
m3: The agent writes a reply in Antares and sends it. Antares delivers it with the Instagram messaging API, using instagram_business_manage_messages, inside the 24-hour messaging window.
m4: On Instagram, the same conversation shows the reply that was sent from Antares.
c1: Antares can reply automatically to comments on the business account's Instagram posts. We create a new automation.
c2: The trigger is a new Instagram comment, with the condition that the comment text contains 'antares test'. The action replies publicly to the comment with this message.
c3: The automation is saved and active. Now a user comments 'antares test' on one of the account's posts.
c4: Antares receives the comment through the Instagram comments webhook, and the automation runs successfully.
c5: On Instagram, the reply is posted under the user's comment. Antares published it using instagram_business_manage_comments.
